name: A website, a store, and a field app
summary: One nonprofit, three live products: a public website with direct donations, a merch store, and a custom field-operations app.
problem: Aloha Animal Outreach conducts monthly outreach to unhoused communities and their pets across O'ahu, but their digital infrastructure couldn't keep up. The website was a dated WordPress build with no donation flow or mobile optimization. Field data lived in six disconnected spreadsheets with no real-time alerts, no case timelines, and no way to flag urgent situations. There was no merch presence and no passive revenue stream beyond one-time donations.
whatIDid:
Designed and built a three-part ecosystem:

Public website: A ground-up rebuild in Astro with direct Stripe donation integration, Netlify Forms for volunteer and partner inquiries, and a new Partners page targeting corporate sponsors.

Field operations app: A custom internal app with a situations-based data model built specifically for animals living long-term with unhoused owners, not the linear intake-to-adoption flow of standard rescue software.

Merch store: A Printful-integrated Shopify store handling passive revenue with zero fulfillment overhead.
outcome: A production-ready public website with direct Stripe donation integration. A fully deployed custom field-operations app replacing six disconnected spreadsheets, now used in monthly outreach operations. A Shopify merch store with zero fulfillment overhead. One client, three live products.

name: An AI recruiting platform, built solo
summary: An AI-powered applicant tracking system built for a tech recruiting firm: candidate sourcing, job-fit scoring, automated triage, and AI-drafted outreach. A 6-phase pipeline keeps AI costs in check.
problem: An independent tech recruiting firm was running candidate sourcing, scoring, and outreach across a set of disconnected tools. Triage was heavily manual, and because every step leaned on AI APIs, the cost of running the pipeline was unpredictable.
whatIDid:
Designed and built an AI-powered applicant tracking system, solo. The workflow runs as a 6-phase pipeline that separates no-cost tasks from paid AI operations, so API spend stays controlled instead of accruing on every step.

Six or more serverless edge functions handle the core work: candidate sourcing, job-fit scoring, automated triage, AI-drafted outreach, and presentation generation. Contact-email extraction from GitHub and Hacker News profiles is automated as part of sourcing.
outcome: In daily production use, running the recruiting firm's candidate pipeline.

name: A client portal, built from scratch
summary: A client portal built for my own practice: onboarding, phase tracking, file approvals, invoicing, and messaging. Live in six weeks.
problem: Running a small design and development practice means managing projects, files, feedback, invoices, and client communication across too many disconnected tools. Every client portal product I evaluated was either too generic, too expensive, or not built for how I actually work.
whatIDid: Designed and built a full-stack client portal from scratch. The portal handles the entire client lifecycle: onboarding, project phase tracking, file delivery with approval workflows, invoice creation and payment, asset uploads, messaging, and email notifications. Clients get a clean, branded experience. I get a single system that runs my practice.
outcome: A live production application at portal.shauna.digital. Every new client I onboard uses it from day one. Built in six weeks alongside active client work.
